title: Kepler's Laws and Orbits
seo_title: Kepler's Laws Worksheets: Ellipses, Equal Areas and T² = a³ (High School Earth Science)
standard_text: Use mathematical or computational representations to predict the motion of orbiting objects in the solar system.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on Kepler's laws and orbits (NGSS HS-ESS1-4): ellipses, equal areas, T² = a³, planet data and orbital speed. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Orbits are ellipses; planets speed up near the Sun; farther planets have longer years.
body_html:
How to think about it

Gravity makes planets follow Kepler's three laws.

  • 1: Orbits are ellipses with the Sun at one focus. 2: Planets move fastest when closest (equal areas in equal times).
  • 3: T² = a³ (T in years, a in AU). Farther planets have much longer years.
  • Orbital speed v = 2πr ÷ T.
Example

a = 4 AU. Period?

T² = 64

T = 8

Answer: 8 years

Example

T = 27 years. Distance?

a³ = 729

a = 9

Answer: 9 AU

Common mistakes

  • Thinking orbits are perfect circles centered on the Sun.
  • Thinking planets move at a constant speed.
  • Using T = a instead of T² = a³.

faq.a: 1: orbits are ellipses with the Sun at one focus. 2: a planet sweeps equal areas in equal times, so it moves faster near the Sun. 3: T² = a³ (years and AU).

faq.q: How do you use T² = a³?
faq.a: Cube the distance in AU and take the square root to get the period in years, or square the period and take the cube root to get the distance.

faq.q: Why do planets speed up near the Sun?
faq.a: The Sun's gravity is stronger there and pulls the planet faster as it falls closer.

space is thinner near the Sun
items.e: Gravity does work on it as it falls closer.

items.q: Why does Mercury speed up as it approaches the Sun?
c: the Sun's gravity pulls harder when it is closer
space is thinner near the Sun
items.e: Gravity does work on it as it falls closer.

items.q: What is Kepler's second law?
c: A line from the Sun to a planet sweeps out equal areas in equal times.
All planets have the same year.

items.q: Why do satellites in low orbit go around Earth faster than the Moon?
c: They are closer, where gravity is stronger.
items.e: Same law for moons and satellites.

items.q: What is an astronomical unit (AU)?
c: the average distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km

items.q: At aphelion (farthest from the Sun), how does an asteroid move compared with the rest of its orbit?
c: It moves at the same speed everywhere.
items.e: Kepler's second law: a line from the Sun sweeps equal areas in equal times, so the planet speeds up when close.

items.q: What is Kepler's third law?
c: The square of a planet's period is proportional to the cube of its average distance (T² = a³).
